req.title: Blog post title required on update
req.statement: The system shall reject POST /<id>/update with a missing title, rendering an error.
triggers: blog post title required on update

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-040 requires that POST /<id>/update rejects a request with a missing title by re-rendering the update form with an error message (HTTP 200, not a redirect). Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — valid update with a non-empty title succeeds (redirects to index, HTTP 302); (2) negative — update with an empty string title is rejected (HTTP 200, error message present, no redirect); (3) boundary — update with a single-character title 'A' (minimum non-empty) is accepted (HTTP 302). Each test sets up its own isolated in-process Flask app with a temp database, logs in as the post author, and makes assertions on exact status codes and response body content to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_update_missing_title_rejected
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /2/update with title='' and body='some body'
expected: Response body contains b'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-040: system shall reject POST /<id>/update with missing title
blog.py update(): if not title: error = 'Title is required.' -> flash(error)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_missing_title_rejected():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # Log in as Rahul (author of post id=2)
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    # POST update with empty title
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': '', 'body': 'some body'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Title is required.' in r.data

test_update_missing_title_rejected()

from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_missing_title_no_db_change():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302

tests.name: test_update_whitespace_only_title_rejected
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /2/update with title='   ' (whitespace only) and body='body'
expected: HTTP 200 (whitespace-only title is falsy after strip, or truthy as raw string — test documents actual SUT behaviour)
If HTTP 200: b'Title is required.' in response (whitespace treated as empty)
If HTTP 302: redirect to '/' (whitespace accepted as non-empty by `if not title`)
trace: R-FLASKR-040: boundary — whitespace-only title; `if not title` in Python is False for '   ', so SUT accepts it
BVA: documents that the SUT does NOT strip whitespace — catches mutations that add .strip()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_whitespace_only_title_boundary():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    # Whitespace-only title: `if not '   '` is False in Python, so SUT accepts it
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': '   ', 'body': 'body'})
    # SUT uses `if not title` — whitespace string is truthy, so redirect expected
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

test_update_whitespace_only_title_boundary()
